subtype: Approach: practising with a friend for motivation [Action]
passage: Every Saturday at ten, Ada carried her violin case across the street in Buenos Aires to Alejandro's house. This Saturday it was drizzling, and she wanted the sofa. She almost texted, "Not today." Then she pictured Alejandro waiting with his rosined bow. She went. They played their scales, took turns with the new piece, and played it for each other. Alejandro clapped at the end, even when the third bar wobbled. Ada walked home under the drizzle, thinking that the sofa would have been comfortable and very boring.

qa.q: What day and time did Ada and Alejandro practise?
qa.a: They practised every Saturday at ten.

qa.q: What was Ada feeling as she nearly texted "Not today"?
qa.a: Ada felt reluctant and tempted to skip it, since she wanted the sofa on a drizzly morning.

qa.q: What could the friends do if one of them is ill, and why?
qa.a: They could play on a video call or move the session to another day, so the routine holds without forcing anyone.

qa.q: How might Alejandro see Ada turning up in the drizzle?
qa.a: Alejandro is probably glad and encouraged, since the friends count on each other to keep the Saturday plan.

grounding: Two friends learning violin agree to practise together on Saturdays and play for each other, which keeps them going.

subtype: Approach: practising with a friend for motivation [Action]
passage: The practice rooms at the community music hall were free on Saturday mornings, and Sangeeta and Pranav had booked room 3, nine to ten, for the whole term. Some Saturdays Sangeeta woke up wanting to pull the blanket over her head. But she knew Pranav would already be at the gate with his violin case, and she'd feel terrible leaving him alone in there. So she went. They took turns: one played the week's piece while the other listened, then said one good thing and one thing to fix. Pranav's bow bounced; Sangeeta rushed the endings. By December neither had missed a single Saturday, and at the winter recital they played a duet.

qa.q: Which room did they book, and when?
qa.a: Room 3, from nine to ten on Saturday mornings.

qa.q: Why did Sangeeta still go on lazy Saturdays, and what was she feeling?
qa.a: She would have felt terrible leaving Pranav alone, so not letting him down mattered more than the blanket.

qa.q: What else could the friends add to their plan?
qa.a: A short midweek call to play one tricky line for each other, so Saturday isn't the only check.

qa.q: How might Pranav experience the arrangement?
qa.a: Pranav gets a reliable partner and honest feedback on his bouncing bow, which helps him improve.

grounding: Two friends learning violin practise together every Saturday and play for each other, which keeps them going even when they feel lazy.

subtype: Approach: practising with a friend for motivation [Action]
passage: I'm Kavitha, Arohi's sister. Every Saturday at four, Arohi's friend Mehr rings our bell with a violin case on her back. They set up in our front room with the music stands facing each other. First Arohi plays the week's piece while Mehr listens with her arms crossed; then they swap. Afterwards they each say something. I've heard "your bow is shaking" and "that bit was beautiful" in the same breath. Last Saturday it was pouring, and Arohi said at lunch she didn't feel like it. At five to four she was still on the sofa. Then the bell rang. Mehr was dripping wet and grinning. Arohi got up without a word and fetched her violin. I don't know if she felt guilty or happy. Maybe both.

qa.q: What time does Mehr ring the bell?
Why might Arohi have got up when the bell rang?
qa.a: She may have felt guilty about making Mehr come through the rain for nothing, and glad to see her.

qa.q: What else could the friends do on very rainy days?
qa.a: Practise over a video call, so the Saturday routine continues without anyone getting soaked.

qa.q: What is the routine like for Mehr?
qa.a: Mehr walks through pouring rain grinning, so the Saturdays clearly matter to her too. 🎻

grounding: A sister watches two friends keep a weekly violin practice together, which gets one of them playing even when she does not feel like it.
